key_insight: Hy-Embodied-VLM-1.0 is an embodied foundation model built to help AI agents perceive, reason, and act effectively in the physical world. Its main idea is to train action-aware capabilities from the start, so the model can adapt better to real-world situations instead of only understanding them.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between multimodal understanding and practical physical-world action. Existing models often recognize what is happening, but struggle to decide what to do next, adapt to changing environments, and interact reliably as embodied agents.
method: Uses an action-centric pre-training strategy to develop agentic skills early in training.
Combines multimodal perception with reasoning about actions and physical-world interaction.
Focuses on efficiency, aiming to produce a powerful embodied model that is practical for real agent deployment.
impact: This matters for AI practitioners because it points toward more capable robots and embodied assistants that can move from passive perception to active decision-making. It also suggests a scalable path for building efficient foundation models for real-world agency.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing perception -> reasoning -> action -> feedback in the physical world.

paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Xumin Yu, Yongming Rao, Yonggen Ling, Yunheng Li
